summary: Observations of SN displacement of luminous points: misinterpretation with the atmospheric reentry of Cosmos 749 rocket.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as type C, which are now being re-examined solely to improve the relevance of the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification in an investigation report. This particular observation was previously classified as type C. On December 25, 1980, between 10:30 PM and 10:45 PM, witnesses observed a series of bluish lights with trails moving along a north-south axis in the sky. The observation lasted 15 seconds. This case is quite consistent (three witnesses, only two of whom were interviewed), and the description of the observed UFO is fairly precise. The witnesses' sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color, trajectory) with an artificial atmospheric reentry. Furthermore, this observation is part of a mass observation of an artificial atmospheric reentry (namely, that of the Cosmos 749 rocket), which occurred within the specified time frame and along the indicated trajectory. It is not the witnesses' visual perception that is at issue, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (astonishment). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UFO A, an observation linked to a misinterpretation of the Cosmos 749 rocket's atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a green luminous phenomenon; downward trajectory.
description: On December 24, 1980, at approximately 12:15 a.m., a witness at home observed a luminous green phenomenon for one to two seconds. This phenomenon appeared to descend from the sky and disappear into the mountains. Despite an inquiry with a ski patrol team working that night and a ground search, no further information has been gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Observation of a round flying object, moving up and down.
description: On December 16, 1980, at approximately 11:00 AM, a witness observed a round object in the sky that he could not identify. This object was topped with a pyramidal antenna; it was metallic in color and dazzled the witness at times. A light yellow halo surrounded it. It moved eastward, making ascending and descending movements. The observation lasted four minutes before the object gradually and completely disappeared in a southerly direction. No further reports were collected by the gendarmerie regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: observation of an oval-shaped object
description: On December 12, 1980, around 5:00 AM, a driver noticed an orange light in her rearview mirror. Approximately 300 meters away in the forest, an oval-shaped object emitted flashing lights that changed from green to red to blue. The witness stopped to observe. This object measured approximately 5 meters wide and 2 meters high. Impressed, the driver continued driving and saw the object disappear at an intersection. No further information or eyewitness accounts were gathered regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: astronomical observation of Venus
description: For several days in a row, a witness observed an orange glow appearing in the east between 6:30 and 8:30 a.m. On December 12, 1980, the gendarmerie brigade decided to observe the luminous phenomenon. Indeed, a glow rose gradually and slowly in the sky. Through prolonged observation, an optical effect set the phenomenon in motion; it changed color with sunrise and continued its ascent. The gendarmes suspected it might be a particular star. The star chart for those days indicated the gradual appearance of Venus in the east, rising and then disappearing with sunrise.

summary: Close observation of a plate-shaped craft. Fear, no noise.
description: On December 3, 1980, around 11:00 PM, a motorist spotted a large, circular object about 150 meters ahead. Fluorescent green in color, it hovered 10 meters above the road. Stopping to observe the object, he noticed it move silently and slowly approach the witness's vehicle. Frightened, the motorist continued driving, passing under the object, which followed him for approximately one kilometer. Reaching an intersection, the motorist observed the object speeding off in the opposite direction. It then quickly disappeared. His observation lasted three to four minutes. During the investigation, another witness reported seeing a blue glow that evening, but his testimony was very brief. Despite an appeal for witnesses and an on-site investigation, no further information was gathered about this unexplained phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a round object on the horizon for a few seconds.
description: On November 28, 1980, between 6:45 and 7:00 a.m., two witnesses spotted a circular orange object on the horizon, rapidly crossing the sky. Their observations lasted only a few seconds. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear movement of a point of light.
description: On November 24, 1980, at approximately 10:20 PM, a motorist spotted a bright white point in the sky for about a second. It moved from west to east in a straight line and was located between 30 and 60 degrees above the horizon. It disappeared instantly. No unusual noise was heard during the observation. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of a disc-shaped object. Very rapid movement.
description: On November 15, 1980, a motorist spotted a strange phenomenon behind some trees on a hill. A disc-shaped object rose in a zigzag pattern across the sky. Brilliantly white, this object moved at high speed. Two beams of light suddenly illuminated the witness's vehicle, startling him. The object quickly disappeared, becoming a single point. No marks were found on the vehicle. At the presumed point of takeoff, no evidence was found on the ground. No further witness accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Observation of the probable re-entry of a meteorite
description: On November 11, 1980, around 6:30 PM, approximately one hundred people across southeastern France and Corsica observed a powerful luminous phenomenon in the sky. Many reports were recorded by the gendarmerie. Hundreds of witnesses in Italy (see the table of Italian cases) and Spain (Catalonia) also reported this extremely spectacular phenomenon. The press also covered the event (see the articles in Nice Matin). Upon receiving a new report of an observation made that day (see BONNIEUX (84)), GEIPAN re-examined the case in order to publish it. A single table compiles the essential elements of the multiple observations (see the investigation report and the table of French testimonies). The numerous witnesses described a very powerful luminous phenomenon that crossed the sky in less than a minute (for most), heading towards the south or southwest. There is considerable variability in the details described, both in the color of the phenomenon (green, red, yellow, purple, white, pink, bluish) and in its shape (sphere, cigar, saucer, triangle, and even parallelepiped), the estimated distance (30m to 2km), the direction of movement (mostly from North to South, or East to West, with some witnesses seeing the opposite direction), and the duration of observation (mostly less than 1 minute, with a few cases exceeding 2 minutes). Experience shows that such variability is common in all mass sightings; it is also important to consider that not all witnesses, being geographically dispersed, saw the phenomenon from the same angle or for the same duration: this leads to a perfectly explainable variability in the witnesses' accounts (see the investigation report). Nevertheless, the simultaneous occurrence of the phenomenon, and certain common characteristics such as its fragmentation into three elements, leave little doubt as to the single origin of the phenomenon. In this type of case, it is the multiplicity of witnesses at the same instant and their significant geographical distance that proves that the phenomenon was very powerful and at high altitude: the atmospheric reentry hypothesis becomes certain. The nature of the reentering object is more difficult to prove: in this case, due to the southwestward orientation of the phenomenon, and its duration of less than one minute, which implies an initial speed well above 10 km/s, the hypothesis of atmospheric reentry by a satellite debris gives way to the hypothesis of a natural meteor reentry. Astronomers from Nice (see the article "The glow in the azure sky: it was indeed a meteorite") and Genoa confirmed this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of an atmospheric reentry of a bolide, caused by a natural meteoroid.

summary: Probable observation of an astral conjunction
description: On October 31, 1980, a motorist returning home from work noticed three bright points of light at a low altitude in the sky. The approximate direction of his observation was northeast (to the left of the vehicle relative to its direction of travel). He had the impression that these points followed him as he moved or stopped at the same time as he did. No sound was heard. At home, his wife made the same observation until 7:30 a.m., the time she left for work. During the investigation, other witnesses to this same phenomenon came forward. An examination of the night sky revealed a conjunction of Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn, particularly visible in the eastern sky and very low on the horizon until sunrise. The witnesses likely observed this phenomenon.

summary: observation of two bright spots from a train
description: On October 31, 1980, at approximately 6:45 a.m., a witness on board a train observed two luminous points that appeared to follow the train's movement. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: observation of Venus and Jupiter
description: On several consecutive evenings between October 30 and November 1, 1980, a witness observed two fixed points of light in the sky. This person was making an astronomical observation of Venus (magnitude -3.91) and Jupiter (magnitude -1.31), which were particularly visible at that time of year.

summary: Observation of bright flashes in the sky followed by a flame and smoke.
description: On October 26, 1980, at approximately 10:35 a.m., a witness, an amateur pilot, observed several flashes of light in the sky from his property, which he thought resembled the flashing lights of an aircraft. He then saw a very bright flame followed by black smoke. No sound was heard. Thinking it might be a plane crash, he alerted the nearest air traffic control tower. During the police investigation, no aircraft in distress was reported in the area, and no rocket launches were detected nearby. No further witness statements were collected regarding this report, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a bright flash every second for 4 minutes: lack of information.
description: On October 22, 1980, at 6:15 PM, a person observed a series of bright flashes in the sky from their home. These lights moved rapidly and appeared white or red. The observation lasted approximately four minutes. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Sighting of a scallop-shaped craft
description: On October 17, 1980, at 11:15 PM, several witnesses saw two powerful spotlights approaching at an altitude of approximately 200 meters. When the spotlights turned left, the witnesses observed a dark craft shaped like a scallop shell with two fixed red lights on its sides. The craft emitted a muffled noise. It is very likely that the witnesses saw an unidentified aircraft, possibly a dirigible.

summary: Nighttime observation by a family of a colored luminous phenomenon on the ground then passing over their home: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named MONTHERME (08) 1980, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On October 12, 1980, a teenage girl went to the gendarmerie to report an observation she had made the previous evening from her home. She reported seeing a UFO in a field 200 meters from her house. The entire family was interviewed. On October 11, 1980, around 11:40 PM, T1 (14 years old) was lying in her room when she saw through the window a sphere on the ground 200 meters away, shaped like a flying saucer or a large cigar with a lighter yellow rim than its orange center. After two minutes of observation, the UFO rose, emitting blue lights and making a motor-like noise, and headed towards La Roche at 7:00 AM. Fifteen to twenty minutes later, it passed over the house again, illuminating the garden in the direction of La Roche. T2 (her sister, 15 years old) went down to T1's room when the latter called her parents. T2 saw a large sphere with a strong yellow light illuminating the garden and the neighbor's garden, and was at La Roche at 7:00 AM, 500 meters away. The UFO remained for a few minutes in the meadow behind the house, then left towards La Roche with a car-like noise. A few minutes later, it passed over the house, heading towards Les Roches. Around 11:30 PM, children T3 and T4 (parents), alerted by T1, saw a long-range, rotating beam of blue light 200-300 meters away for 10-15 minutes. A short, muffled starting sound was heard by T3 (but not T4). The sphere was not seen by T3 and T4 as it was hidden by trees. The police found no trace at the scene, nor any related sightings in the neighborhood. These accounts are truly strange only in what is testified by children T1 and T2, who say they saw the sphere that produced the lights, both on the ground and in the air above the house. This is probably the reason for the initial classification of the case in D. The present re-examination notes this strong strangeness but also the low level of consistency of the testimonies insofar as nothing allows us to understand why the parents did not see the ball on the ground or in the air. - For T1 and T2, the UFO remained on the ground for only two or a few minutes before taking off, while T3 and T4, who necessarily began their observation after T1, were able to observe (therefore in the company of T1) rotating lights and beams for 15 minutes. The origin of these beams was not visible ("hidden by trees" for T4) and was implicitly or explicitly (for T4) on the ground or nearby. - T3 and T4 therefore stopped their observation without ever having seen the UFO take off. T3 does not specify what constituted the end of his observation, while for T4, it was the extinction of the lights on the ground that led him to return to his room. - For T1 and T2, the startup noise is associated with the UFO's ascent and the beginning of its flight. For T3, the noise is associated with the beginning of his observation of lights that never actually rose, and for T4 (who did not hear the noise (but says he's a little hard of hearing) understood that the noise came later, once he had returned to his room. - It is necessary to rule out the possibility that the UFO had already left by the time the parents (T3 and T4) arrived and that they were focused on residual lights on the ground. Indeed, T1 and T2 do not mention residual lights on the ground and would have drawn the parents' attention to the strangeness in the sky, and the parents would then have seen it, as T1 and T2 did, passing over the house again. - It is curious that the parents, T3 and T4, describe lights seen (on the ground) without referring in their deposition to the testimony of the flying UFO seen by their children, even if only to place the observations sequentially or to report their children's emotions and statements. There is a kind of distance between the parents and the children's testimonies. They stick strictly to what they saw. - It is also noted that the testimony was The report was initiated by child T1 at the gendarmerie. The gendarmerie then requested statements from other witnesses. T4 (the father) refused an initial summons to the gendarmerie. There are too many inconsistencies between the testimonies to validate the main strangeness of the observation, which consists of these lights, balls, or cigar-shaped objects that take off and fly over the area. The most likely explanation is that there were indeed lights on the ground for an unknown reason. The observation of flying lights is highly suspicious. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a few seconds of a bright white UFO moving in an arc then vertically taking the shape of an upside-down plate: lack of reliable information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D (and also known as MONTAUBAN (82) 1980), is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On October 6, 1980, at 6:00 a.m., a motorist stopped at a stop saw a luminous object emitting a white, neon-like light at low altitude. Shaped like a rocket, this craft moved in an arc above the houses. After a brief pause, the object moved vertically and appeared to the witness as an inverted plate. The object then disappeared completely. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted only a few seconds. No other witness accounts of this phenomenon were collected. The witness provided numerous unusable details (size or diameter of 1.5 meters, distance of approximately 50 meters, speed comparable to that of a watch second hand) in the absence of angular reference points or known landmarks. If we exclude these details from the analysis, very little of the testimony remains that can be used. It can thus be summarized as follows: - observation for a few seconds of a luminous white UFO in the shape of a rocket moving silently in an arc, then pausing, moving vertically in an inverted plate shape, and disappearing. We can also deduce from the testimony that the UFO was probably at a low angular height above the horizon: it was at the height of trees or rooftops. Although the police went to the scene, no other usable information was gathered. It would have been helpful to clarify the following points: - the witness's exact position in their car. Were they in front of their home or elsewhere? - the exact azimuths of the UFO's appearance and disappearance; - the starting and ending elevations; - the angular size of the UFO; - how exactly did the UFO disappear? Did it suddenly go out on the spot, or gradually? Or did the witness lose sight of the UAP? Given the unknowns and missing parameters, we cannot rule out a helicopter in flight on the horizon, the movement of a bird illuminated by a searchlight, or even a much stranger phenomenon. This lack of data prevents further analysis. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: probable sighting of an aircraft towing a brightly lit advertisement
description: On October 5, 1980, between 7:25 PM and 8:00 PM, several witnesses observed a curious object moving at low altitude. Described as circular or rectangular, it emitted lights. It moved very slowly and silently, making back-and-forth movements. Witnesses observed this object in the sky for over fifteen minutes. It then disappeared in the direction of Belgium. During the investigation, it was noted that that same evening that a Belgian aircraft, with unusual lighting on its wings and fuselage, was towing a luminous advertisement.

summary: Sighting of a flying saucer.
description: On September 23, 1980, at 4:15 a.m., two people returning from work spotted a flying saucer taking off behind the village church. As it rose rapidly, it emitted beams of light that dazzled the witnesses. This craft was seen again by one of the two people above a forest. No other witness accounts or traces behind the church were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of various lights, probably from a nighttime car race
description: On the night of September 20-21, 1980, numerous witnesses, including military personnel, repeatedly saw luminous orbs moving along varying trajectories, disappearing and reappearing suddenly. The sky was heavily overcast and the weather was very stormy. That night, a car race was taking place on the slopes of nearby Mont Ventoux. Although the investigation did not prove it, the hypothesis of reflections of car headlights in the night sky and on the low clouds can be seriously considered, with the various trajectories and successive appearances and disappearances explained by the topography of the racetrack.

summary: probable astronomical observation of Acturus.
description: On September 15, 1980, between 7:40 PM and 9:30 PM, several people observed a luminous phenomenon from their homes. A bright point, larger than a star, changed in intensity and color before disappearing in the northwest. These people likely made an astronomical observation of Acturus, which was particularly visible (magnitude 0.15) at that time of year.

summary: Black cylindrical object with sudden acceleration
description: On September 14, 1980, at 12:45 PM, an aerial traffic controller on duty observed a peculiar phenomenon. Directly above the controller, a black, cylindrical object remained stationary. The object, located approximately 300 meters above the ground, then suddenly accelerated and disappeared, heading east. No information allowing for a serious study of this observation has been collected.

summary: Observation of an elongated object moving in jerks
description: In the early hours of September 10, 1980, at approximately 12:45 a.m., a witness on his doorstep observed a luminous phenomenon. About 100 meters along the path leading to his home, a glow illuminated a road sign. No cars or other noises were heard, and the witness then saw an elongated object moving jerkily about 1.5 meters above the ground. This object gradually rose and disappeared into the landscape. No unusual odor was detected. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Sighting of a strange object 150m above the ground: lack of information
description: On the night of September 5th, a little girl got up to close her bedroom window, which had been opened by a gust of wind. Outside, she saw a luminous object in the sky about 100 meters from her home. This object was semi-circular and emitted a very bright yellow-orange light. It hovered about 150 meters above the ground. Several times, the object went dark, leaving a light on at each end. The observation lasted about half an hour without the object touching the ground, and then it went dark completely. The child made no further observations, and no other accounts were collected about this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Multiple observations above the ocean of two bright red balls with trails: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named LANNION (22) 1980, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On September 5, 1980, at 10:45 PM, eight witnesses were surprised by a luminous phenomenon over the ocean. Of these eight witnesses, only three were interviewed by the relevant gendarmerie on September 8, 1980. During their interviews, witnesses T1 and T2 described two very bright red spheres leaving a trail in the sky. The passengers in the vehicle (T1 and T2) had the impression that these spheres were approaching and following them. Frightened, they sought refuge at the home of a resident (T3) of Plestin-les-Grèves (22), who also saw a very bright red sphere at the top of the fir trees bordering the cemetery. Her observation lasted a few seconds, then she brought everyone inside to reassure them. The appearance of the UFOs as described by the witnesses (sphere shape, red color, strong brightness, presence of a trail) perfectly matches the main working hypothesis, namely a confusion with two parachute-type distress flares (see the investigation report). The initial observation placed the UFOs over the ocean, in or near the bay of Saint-Michel-des-Grèves, which strengthens the hypothesis that such rockets are launched from the ocean. Regarding the behavior of the UFOs in relation to this hypothesis, the illusion of a following sphere, for distant objects, explains the impression that witnesses, while traveling in their vehicles, had that the UFOs were following them, stopping when they did the same, etc. The other characteristic of UFO behavior is the magnification noted by witnesses, interpreted as an approach to their vehicle, which is not necessarily the case. This could very well be explained by an increase in the brightness of the rockets, once the illuminating charge is triggered, making them appear artificially larger, and therefore seem closer. The only remaining inconsistency with this hypothesis concerns the duration. Although the eyewitness accounts regarding the initial observation position at Saint-Efflam can be interpreted in two different ways, both valid, the time taken by the witnesses to travel the distance between their initial observation point and their final point (corresponding to the observation duration, between 60 and 90 seconds) is longer than the visibility period of the distress parachute flares, which never exceeds 45 seconds. Various hypotheses have been put forward to try to explain this inconsistency. One of them particularly caught our attention: the possibility of two successive launches of two parachute flares. Since these flares become visible once they reach apogee, and are launched in the same direction, they could be seen, from the witnesses' position, in the same place in the sky. Furthermore, during the second launch, visibility was reduced (the rockets were observed from the rear of the vehicle), and panic spread inside the vehicle. The witnesses likely did not notice the transition between the two launches, as the general confusion impaired their judgment. Unfortunately, we lack reliable and precise data to support this hypothesis. The witness accounts are indeed imprecise, particularly regarding the duration of observation of the different phases. We would also have liked more details concerning any interruptions in observation by either witness during the journey. Such information is unverifiable more than 35 years after the events. Although inconsistencies related to the observation period can theoretically be explained, in practice the lack of precise data prevents classification as eBe, as there is a possible confusion with parachute-type distress flares. Consequently, the appropriate classification for this case is C e, as the lack of data does not allow for a sufficiently robust assessment.

summary: Observation of a flat disk emitting beams of light.
description: On September 5, 1980, at 6:15 a.m., a witness observed a circular object, one meter in diameter, in the sky at an altitude of 200 meters. The object, a violet disc, emitted beams of light. The observation lasted five minutes before the witness left. No military maneuvers were conducted in that area that day. No further reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: observation of Venus.
description: On September 12, 1980, at 4:28 a.m., gendarmes on patrol observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. For an hour and a half, a luminous sphere located in the northeast moved slowly. This sphere was yellow and exhibited variations in intensity. The weather was very clear, visibility was excellent, and there was no moon. These individuals made an astronomical observation of Venus, which was particularly visible (magnitude 4.15) at that time of year.

summary: Observation of a metallic grey sphere in the sky during the launch of an experimental rocket: probable observation of a balloon.
description: An old observation (1980) but recently reported (2015). During a summer camp themed around "experimental rockets" organized by ANSTJ, a witness observed, through binoculars, the disappearance of a rocket named Fuch Off, which appeared to be absorbed by a spherical object itself being pursued by two fighter jets. This observation report is quite unusual: firstly, it concerns an old observation, from 1980, reported to GEIPAN in July 2015; secondly, this observation relates to a launch operation of educational micro-rockets under the responsibility of CNES and ANSTJ. GEIPAN conducted an internal CNES investigation to identify the participants or witnesses of this event. The investigation proved quite difficult after 35 years, but it was nevertheless possible to locate one of those responsible for this rocket launch operation, who still possessed all the launch records from that period. He wrote a detailed report of the launch (see his report). The rocket was not recovered due to the particularly dense vegetation on the site. The report makes no mention of the sphere described by the witness. The fighter jets did indeed fly over the area at that time, but were unrelated to the Fuch Off rocket launch. GEIPAN has no other hypothesis for the silver sphere than a possible case of mistaken identity with a pilot balloon (a small-diameter balloon whose trajectory, observed from the ground, indicates wind speed and direction). The coincidence of the rocket launch, the sphere's passage, and the fighter jets' flight appears to be purely coincidental. Because the operations manager did not mention any particular problem or any other report of this silver sphere despite the large number of spectators, GEIPAN consequently classifies this case in category B, as a probable case of mistaken identity with a ball.

summary: Sightings of a gigantic rectangular craft flying over and following a vehicle: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named SAINT-ETIENNE (04) 1980, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On August 30th at 1:30 PM, a witness on patrol was driving his vehicle when he noticed a flash of light in the sky. Looking up, he saw above his vehicle a "gigantic object," matte, rectangular in shape and gold-grey in color. The witness described the presence of two rows of black dots on the left side, as well as a yellow and red triangle at the front. Another triangle was described on the right side. The UFO seemed to follow the car during slowdowns, accelerations, and changes of direction. The driver lost sight of it several times. The witness's 6-year-old daughter was in the car: she gave the same description as her father and was the last to see the UFO over the village before it suddenly disappeared into the sky "without taking a specific direction." According to the available information, this sighting is strange for several reasons (see the investigation report): The apparently very large angular size of the UFO, with witnesses describing it in these terms: - T1: to gigantic to; to immense to; It could have covered between 1 and 1 hectare. It was perhaps 100 or 150 meters above the ground; the device obscured the sky; - T2: large device, T2, rear passenger of the car, also made a drawing where the UFO above the car protruded on either side of the car's roof. It is very surprising, if the UFO was as imposing as the witnesses described, that no other testimony was brought to the attention of the police, especially since the observation took place during the day, over a probably quite long period of time, and along a trajectory of several kilometers. With the available information, no known meteorological, astronomical, or aeronautical phenomenon can account for the characteristics of the UFO as described by the witnesses. In the current GEIPAN methodology (since 2008, see the website GEIPAN Classification Methodology), for a strange observation to be considered as such and classified as unexplained, there must be significant consistency, meaning a high level of information and reliability is required. In terms of information, the lack of a more thorough investigation by the gendarmerie, beyond the necessary but unsuccessful questioning of local residents, is regrettable, in order to find other potential witnesses. We would have liked to have the following information: a sketch of the UFO made independently by T1; Photographs of the key locations mentioned by T1, as part of an investigation reconstructing the trajectory of the witness's vehicle; measurements of the angular dimensions of the UFO and its components; more details on the UFO's disappearances: at what precise moment, and in what manner (gradual extinction, sudden rapid departure, etc.); the same remarks on the UFO's reappearances: did the witnesses actually observe a reappearance (in what manner?) or did they simply look at the UFO, which was already present? Regarding the UFO itself: was it visible against a blue sky? Against a cloudy background? If so, was it, at any point, partially or totally obscured by clouds? Did the entire UFO appear solid to the witnesses, or did it have less perceptible, more blurred, difficult-to-distinguish parts? At one point in his account, T1 states that the UFO was visible above the Villerme woods (located to the right of the road taken by the witnesses). It was therefore no longer above the vehicle at that moment. The same is true for T2, who briefly glimpsed the UFO above the village at the moment when, having arrived home, T1 parked the vehicle in the garage. It would have been interesting to have more details about the appearance of the UFO, its altitude above the horizon, its angular dimensions, etc., at these precise moments of the observation. In terms of reliability, the testimony of a 6-year-old child, without providing any decisive additional information compared to that of the father, does not significantly increase the reliability of the father's testimony, especially when the circumstances of the child's interview are unknown (presence or name of the father). Overall, the evidence is insufficient (especially in terms of information) to classify this seemingly strange observation as unexplained. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: OBSERVATION OF AN OBJECT CHANGING SHAPE. SUDDEN DISAPPEARANCE.
description: On August 29, 1980, at approximately 8:50 PM, two witnesses on their terrace observed a peculiar phenomenon in the sky. Coming from the west, a black sphere, seen against the light, passed at high speed directly above the house. The witnesses then saw its shape change and perceived about a dozen square-shaped windows that appeared to be illuminated from within. An intense light suddenly appeared, and the entire object disappeared to the east. The entire observation lasted 20 to 30 seconds without any noise being heard. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry
description: On August 25, 1980, between 9:25 PM and 10:00 PM, several witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. A colored, circular shape moved without any unusual noise being heard. The witnesses, located in the city, lost sight of the object, which was hidden by buildings. The observation was very brief, but the witnesses stated that the object emitted luminous radiation. The Pic du Midi Observatory was contacted, but nothing unusual was observed. It is likely that the witnesses witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observing a stationary object in the sky
description: On August 24, 1980, a witness observed a very bright shape in the sky at 3:30 a.m. The intense brightness made observation difficult, but the witness did see a slightly pinkish, parachute-like shape detach from beneath the object. This parachute remained visible for only a few seconds; however, the witness observed the luminous sphere for more than 10 minutes before going back to bed. When he awoke a few hours later, everything had disappeared. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observations of an object of "polished aluminum" color that oscillates on itself and moves: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named SAINT-MARTIN-DE-CRAU (13) 24.08.1980, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On August 24, 1980, around 8:00 PM, two witnesses in their garden were intrigued by the presence of an object in the air. Witnesses described a bowl-shaped object, polished aluminum in color. The upper part of the object appeared to oscillate, while the lower part seemed stationary. The object descended vertically, then slowly, heading towards a field and crossing the RN113 highway. The object then moved north on a horizontal trajectory, and the witness lost sight of it. No noise or smoke was observed. No other witness statements were collected by the gendarmerie. During the on-site investigation by the gendarmerie, no particular findings were made, as the object never landed. The object's movement in accordance with the wind direction suggests it may have been a type of balloon, possibly made of Mylar, which could explain the polished aluminum color. Mylar balloons were already in use at that time. However, the descriptions provided by witnesses and the sketches made by the police (not by the witnesses) do not allow us to determine what type of balloon it might have been. The shape is indeed relatively complex, with unusual features. To gain a better understanding, and to confirm or refute the hypothesis of a Mylar balloon or something else, we would have liked to have more concrete information, which is not included in the police report, such as: - angular measurements of the UFO (Unidentified Floating Object). - a drawing made by the witnesses, not the police. - estimates of angular heights at the beginning, middle, and end of the observation. - color measurements using, for example, a Pantone color chart. Although a balloon hypothesis can be formulated, the lack of consistency in the witness testimony, despite the on-site investigation by the police, prevents us from drawing a conclusion. Consequently, Geipan classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of a spherical craft.
description: On August 23, 1980, at approximately 9:30 a.m., a witness observed a flash of light from their home. They then made an observation that intrigued them: a very bright, spherical flying object was moving across the sky. Approaching a mountain range, the object tilted on its edge, turned red, and quickly disappeared behind the landscape to the north. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: long observations two days in a row of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: astronomical observation of Venus.
description: On August 23 and 25, 1980, at approximately 3:30 a.m., a witness observed a very bright point of light from their fourth-floor apartment, positioned in the same place in the sky. The witness described this point as a stationary star that appeared to be in the east. On August 25, the observation continued for about two hours with binoculars before the phenomenon disappeared, its brightness gradually decreasing. No further reports were collected by the gendarmerie. This case of observation (under the name BOUSSY-SAINT-ANTOINE (91) 08/23/1980) is classified as a Category C case by GEPAN, although the hypothesis of an observation of the planet Venus was considered probable at the time. This case was recently re-examined (see the document "Investigation Notes"). This case is inconsistent (single witness), but the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the planet Venus, which was particularly visible at the time of observation (magnitude -4.26). Furthermore, Venus was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky (the possibility of mistaking it for Venus had been raised by GEPAN). The issue is not the witness's visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their own experience (fatigue, nighttime observation). In GEIPAN's current classification, this case of a weak unusual object is classified as Ae, an observation linked to a misidentification of Venus.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent movement of a red-orange ball with a trail in the night sky: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named CHANAZ (73) 22.08.1980, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On August 22, 1980, at approximately 9:45 PM, a witness was drawn outside his home by a bright flash. He observed a round, orange-red burst of lightning with a tail in the sky. The phenomenon moved quickly and silently along a straight trajectory. No odor was detected. Only one eyewitness account was collected on August 24, 1980. Based on its visual appearance and trajectory, the described UFO is perfectly consistent with the atmospheric reentry of a meteor or a satellite (see the investigation report). The observation duration is not described but can be indirectly estimated at a minimum of 10 seconds and a maximum of 1 or 2 minutes. It is consistent with a long-duration meteor reentry, following a trajectory tangential to the atmosphere (a rare phenomenon, but one that has been observed for durations of up to two minutes), as well as with the reentry of a satellite (the latter always using a tangential trajectory). What reduces the probability of the hypothesis, without invalidating it, is the fact that there were no other eyewitness accounts, even though such a UFO had time to fly over a large geographical area, was large, bright, and visible for at least 10 seconds, and occurred at a time of night, albeit relatively late during the summer and holiday season. The consistency is mediocre. It could have been improved by an interview with the witness to obtain a more precise angular measurement in azimuth and elevation, and especially to obtain a much more accurate indication of the observation time than the interview could only indirectly estimate. This consistency is just sufficient to support the atmospheric reentry hypothesis, despite the lingering strangeness linked to the lack of observation by other witnesses of such a long and luminous reentry. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid or a satellite craft.

summary: Observation of a small hot air balloon catching fire.
description: On August 19, 1980, at approximately 9:30 PM, a group of young people observed a luminous mass moving slowly and swaying across the sky. This light-colored object had a rounded, luminous upper section. It was at the altitude of light aircraft flights and was moving from north to south. Suddenly, the object burst into flames and plummeted to the ground, leading witnesses to believe it had crashed nearby, though they were unable to pinpoint the exact location. The police later recovered part of the object caught in a tree. The debris allowed them to determine that the object was a hot air balloon made of tissue paper and wire, constructed by an amateur. The owner of the object was never found.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous crescent-shaped phenomenon that seems to follow the witnesses: astronomical misinterpretation of the Moon.
description: On Sunday, August 17, 1980, at approximately 10:00 PM, in a forester's lodge, two witnesses were intrigued by a very bright phenomenon to the west. Seen through binoculars, a large crescent-shaped object emitted intense beams of light. Deciding to investigate this luminous phenomenon more closely, the witnesses took a vehicle and continued to see the crescent, which appeared to move rapidly and follow their vehicle. Becoming frightened, the witnesses decided to turn back and return home. The luminous phenomenon, after coming to a stop, disappeared. No trace was found on the ground or on the vegetation, and no other witness was able to provide further information. This old case, classified as "D," was recently re-examined (see the Investigation Note). This case is consistent (2 witnesses), the description of the observation site and the observed UFO is quite precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color, etc.) with a known astronomical object: the Moon at sunset. Furthermore, the Moon was indeed present in the observed area of the sky, even though the witnesses did not mention it. The issue is not the witnesses' visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (fatigue, anxiety, and fear). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a weak anomaly is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misinterpretation of the Moon.

summary: Quick observations by a motorist and his passenger of 3 human-like shapes in the vehicle's headlights: lack of information.
description: On August 17, 1980, at 1:30 a.m., two witnesses were driving on National Route 1. Upon reaching Cap Houssaye, they briefly glimpsed three motionless human figures on a hill overlooking the sea, about fifteen meters from the roadside. These figures, illuminated by their headlights, were described as being approximately two meters tall with a heavy build, and having orange, oval-shaped swellings on their heads. No unusual noises were heard. The following evening, one of the witnesses saw a very bright blue light on the ocean from their home, in the direction of Cap Houssaye, towards the location of the sighting. The witnesses only reported this to the police on August 30. Dispatched immediately to the scene, the police found no evidence in the area. GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named SAINT-GILLES (974) 1980, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. The initial unexplained D classification can be understood by a witness's (T2) opposition to the divers hypothesis. However, the reported features of normal human forms, aside from their glare in headlights and large orange eyes, do support this hypothesis. The possibility of divers near the coast in the middle of the night in August in Réunion is plausible, even in the apparent absence of a parked vehicle on the road. We note that the frightened witnesses did not stop to observe the evolution of these forms, nor did they look for a parked vehicle nearby. In the absence of any justification from the witness for their objection, this is the hypothesis that should be considered. But the observation of a ground phenomenon without an associated description of a phenomenon observed in the sky or at the interface between sky and earth (aerospace) falls outside the GEIPAN's remit. Even though the diver hypothesis is highly plausible, GEIPAN prefers to classify the case as unexploitable at its level. The case is classified as Class C.

summary: Observation of a luminous mushroom-cap shaped object
description: On August 16, 1980, at approximately 3:30 a.m., while returning from a village dance, a witness observed a mushroom-shaped object over a field. About 15 meters in diameter, it emitted a bright red light. After approaching to within about 400 meters, the witness became frightened and fled. During his escape, he observed the object flying over the village, still emitting red light and remaining completely silent. No traces were found on the ground or vegetation. No explanation has been found for this sighting.

summary: Observations of a light source in the sky: probable astronomical observations of Mercury
description: On August 14, 1980, at 4:45 a.m., witnesses observed a light source low on the horizon. Emitting a shimmering yellow light and moving very slowly, this phenomenon was observed for several minutes before disappearing, diminishing in intensity and size. During the police investigation, other witnesses were found: it is likely that these people had made an astronomical observation of Mercury, which was particularly visible at that time of year.

summary: Probable atmospheric re-entry
description: On August 9, 1980, at 10:18 PM, two witnesses observed a glow in the sky from their home. It moved from north to south, then changed direction to the southwest, following a curve. It had a circular shape with a very bright core. It also changed color, going from yellowish-white to a hazy red. No noise was heard during the observation. The glow suddenly disappeared. No other reports were collected regarding what appears to have been a possible atmospheric reentry.

summary: observations of a silent, rapidly moving luminous phenomenon.
description: On August 7th, at 9:40 PM and again at 10:45 PM, several witnesses saw a yellow-orange luminous phenomenon pass over a radio station at the Taverny Naval Base. Each time, it moved at very high speed and gained altitude. No sound was heard. No traces of it were found on the vegetation at the site. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of two groups of three lights forming a triangle with engine noise.
description: On August 6, 1980, around 11:00 PM, three people observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon in the sky. For two to five minutes, they watched two groups of three red lights, one of which was flashing. These two groups followed each other closely. The sound of an engine accompanied the group, which moved at low altitude and slow speed. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected. The investigation revealed that at the time of the observation, numerous aircraft were using this air corridor. However, this phenomenon remains unexplained due to a lack of information.

summary: Likely sighting of aircraft.
description: On August 5, 1980, around 11:00 PM, people observed an object moving from east to west in the sky. This elongated object emitted a central light. It suddenly changed direction, heading due south and then due east. Later that same evening, witnesses reported seeing other similar objects. On August 6, around 11:45 PM, an object flying towards the northeast was sighted. No further reports were collected. The Bele/Mulhouse airport reported numerous flights that evening. The witnesses likely observed an aircraft.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere.
description: On July 24, 1980, two witnesses returning home around 4:30 a.m. spotted a very bright white ball in the sky. It emitted an intense light that illuminated the countryside. This ball rose and headed north after making a right-angle turn. It then hovered, and the witnesses were able to observe this phenomenon for an hour despite the intense brightness that hurt their eyes. They went to bed but heard crackling sounds. Photographs taken by one of the witnesses could not be used: the film was declared "burned" by the photographer, who refused to develop it. One of the witnesses reported seeing this very bright white ball again later that same day. No other witnesses in the vicinity came forward. No further information has been gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of an orange hemisphere in the NW sky: astronomical observation of the Sun.
description: This sighting is classified as a C case by GEPAN, under the name SAINT-CYR L'ECOLE (78) 21.07.1980. It was recently re-examined (see the Investigation Notes document). On July 21, 1980, at 6:25 a.m., a witness observed an orange glow in the clear sky from his 5th-floor apartment. Moving onto his balcony, he then distinguished a bright orange hemisphere. This object remained stationary for a minute before moving in a straight line and disappearing. No other information was gathered by the gendarmerie. This case is not very substantial (single witness, short observation), but the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Sun. Furthermore, the Sun was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky. The issue is not the witness's visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their own experience (observing the Sun through clouds). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a weak anomaly is classified as Ae, an observation linked to a misidentification of the Sun.

summary: Observation of a circular disk, moving slowly and silently
description: On July 4, 1980, shortly before 10:30 PM, a witness observed a very bright orange disc in the sky. A wisp of smoke accompanied the disc to its right. The entire object moved silently. After less than a minute of observation, the disc disappeared, leaving behind a yellow light. No further information has been gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of a triangular object moving silently: lack of information.
description: On June 19, 1980, at 11:45 PM, a child's room lit up, and he saw a triangular-shaped object through the window. Steady or flashing lights illuminated the object, which moved silently. The base of the object was lit yellow, and alternating yellow and red lights on the sides flashed. A bright red beacon illuminated when the side lights reached the top. Frightened, the child called his mother, and together they watched the object disappear into the landscape. The sky was cloudy at the time of the sighting. No further information has been gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: observation of a luminous object in the sky
description: On June 6, 1980, three officers on patrol observed a curious object at 2:00 a.m. crossing the sky from west to east in a straight line at high speed. The object was rounded at the front and pointed at the rear, and shone like a neon light. The observation lasted four seconds before the object disappeared over the horizon. No noise of movement or falling was heard. No other information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of a stationary luminous shape.
description: On the night of July 25, 1980, at approximately 2:45 a.m., a witness reported seeing an orange, oval-shaped luminous object, approximately 0.80 meters high and 0.40 meters wide, about 50 meters from his home. This stationary luminous mass was observed by the witness for 40 minutes. The glow disappeared as the witness entered his kitchen. No trace of it was found on the ground. Another person reported witnessing a luminous sphere a month earlier, 50 meters above the ground, which moved while following their vehicle. No further information has been gathered regarding these phenomena, about which we lack details.

summary: Observation of a dome-shaped object.
description: On May 26, 1980, around 7:00 PM, two walkers spotted an unusual object in the clear sky. One of the witnesses, a flight engineer, described an object with a metallic appearance, round in base, and shaped, in its upper part, like a silvery dome. The object, hovering 200 to 300 meters above the ground, appeared to oscillate on its axis. Its lower part was darker and intermittently displayed a reddish luminescence. During six minutes of observation, no noise or condensation was noticed. The object disappeared into the clouds, leveling off in successive stages. A radar echo was recorded at the Belém/Mulhouse airport, but it was obscured by private and general air traffic and therefore of little use. No other witnesses or information were gathered, either in France or in the German border area. This phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: observation of distress flares.
description: On May 26, 1980, at approximately 10:45 PM, several witnesses, including police officers, observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. Two circular, red objects descended slowly toward the ground at a constant speed. Then, red glows appeared, rising into the air before disappearing. Some witnesses reported seeing reddish smoke. The investigation revealed that that evening, individuals had launched distress flares intended for boats, without malicious intent, as these flares were no longer up to standard and could no longer be used at sea.

summary: Observation of the probable reentry of an object into the atmosphere.
description: On May 15, 1980, at 12:30 a.m., a witness observed a luminous, oval-shaped object rapidly descending across the sky. Reddish-orange in color, it was followed by a tail. The object's brightness was far greater than that of a star. It disappeared while moving westward. No other reports of this phenomenon have been collected. This person likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On May 13, 1980, at approximately 4:45 a.m., a witness walking to work was startled by the appearance of a very bright green sphere in the sky. It moved along a south-north trajectory at a very low altitude. This sphere was followed by a shower of yellow sparks. The observation lasted less than 5 seconds, and no sound was heard. No other reports of this phenomenon have been collected. This person likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a luminous object seemingly following the witnesses' vehicle: astronomical mistake with Venus.
description: On May 13, 1980, at 12:05 AM, two gendarmes patrolling the A1 motorway spotted a luminous object above the Roye toll plaza (80). Intrigued, they continued to a rest area parking lot and then radioed their command post, where another gendarme confirmed the object's presence in the sky. One of the witnesses took two photos of the UFO, but the film development proved negative. Resuming their vehicle and heading north, the gendarmes noticed that the UFO appeared to be following the car. The observation lasted nearly an hour. This sighting was classified as a C case in 1980 by GEPAN (Group for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena). It is currently being re-examined (see Investigation Note). This case is consistent (two primary witnesses and two secondary witnesses), and the description of the observation location and the observed UFO is precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color, etc.) with a known astronomical object: Venus at sunset. Furthermore, Venus was indeed present in the observed area of the sky, even though the witnesses did not mention it. The issue is not the witnesses' visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (impression of being followed, night driving). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misidentification of Venus.

summary: Observation of a plate-shaped object. Impression of a human presence in the witness's room.
description: On May 8, 1980, at 11:30 p.m., police were called to the scene of a strange phenomenon. A witness, deeply shaken, claimed that his room was suddenly illuminated by a bright light, that he felt the presence of a humanoid figure in the room, and that he and his sister saw a luminous object moving through the window. The police found no evidence or other testimonies in the area to corroborate these accounts. Other witnesses, present at home in rooms with good lighting, should have seen the phenomenon given its magnitude. This was not the case. The witnesses' guard dogs, usually very aggressive at night at the slightest light, did not react during this event. Finally, the police investigation revealed a certain fragility in the witness. The most likely hypothesis is therefore that the witness was probably misled by luminous phenomena coming from vehicles easily visible from the bedroom window while he was probably in a state of particular sensitivity to supernatural phenomena.

summary: Observation of an object resembling two upside-down bowls placed one on top of the other. Effects on animals.
description: On May 8, 1980, at approximately 9:15 PM, alerted by her frightened dog and the neighborhood dogs barking unusually, a witness saw a peculiar object above her neighbors' house. This object resembled a large child's spinning top, rotating on its axis while moving in a north-south direction. The inside of the device was reddish-orange. Two other people also witnessed the event. All three observed that the images on their television sets had disappeared at that moment, replaced by static. No other accounts of this sighting were collected. This phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Observations of a bright, whitish luminous phenomenon at low altitude; front-to-back displacement effect: observation of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named TOURNON (07) 1980, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On May 8, 1980, at approximately 10:30 PM, soldiers conducting night shooting exercises observed a peculiar phenomenon above the training ground. Their attention was drawn to a point emitting a bright white light. Witnesses described an object to the west moving in their direction, approaching and receding silently. The observation period was long before the object disappeared to the west. These testimonies from career military personnel, as recorded in the police report, present the characteristics of a UFO sighting. These characteristics are now well-known to GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) due to the accumulation of explained cases of this type, particularly over the last ten years (see www.geipan.fr and search for cases related to celestial phenomena such as Venus, the Moon, and the Sun): - long observation period of more than 30 minutes, low altitude in the sky, near-stationary or very short trajectory. Indeed, none of the witnesses described any angular change in the UFO's position, even though the observation lasted over an hour. - sensation of the UFO moving back and forth. The witness, having interpreted the celestial body as a nearby object, logically interpreted any variation in its brightness as a movement forward or backward, with the object maintaining a constant intensity. T2 said, "This point of light must have been quite a distance away, above the mountain! This point approached, until it became the size of a football; it was very bright. It stopped facing us, in the direction of the targets, and its brightness noticeably illuminated the area where we were standing. I should point out that the sky where this object was located was completely clear of clouds." T1 said, "This object then moved away at a much faster speed than it had come. When this craft left, we continued our firing session. Ten to twelve minutes after moving away, this craft returned but at a much greater distance." - Witnesses failed to identify a remarkable celestial body, very bright yet present in the direction of observation, while the sky was described as clear and starry. It was verified that it was indeed a celestial body, namely Venus. The direction of Venus (moving from azimuth 290° to azimuth 300°) is consistent with the observation of T1, the only witness to provide the direction: "This phenomenon came from the west. It moved away in the same direction" (the west-east movement being the approach-movement illusion previously described). The first misconception, which leads to the second (a back-and-forth movement), lies in the failure to recognize the celestial body. Venus is the source of many misconceptions. It is by far the brightest star (here, magnitude -4.5), visible at low elevations in the sky (here, from 16th to 11th), and its rays pass through a thick atmospheric layer, producing varying effects such as changes in brightness, color distortion, halos, and even oscillations due to atmospheric turbulence. Here, the UFO appears yellow or white, and with varying intensities. All these effects exist even in the absence of clouds and can be accentuated (variations in intensity, even to near disappearance) by the presence of otherwise invisible cloud cover. We verified that Venus was indeed visible, taking into account the surrounding mountains: the significant obstacle in the direction of Venus from the firing range was Mont Rosier or Cerisier at 700 m altitude, representing a difference in elevation of approximately 200 m from the firing range, which is over 1.5 km away, or an angle of 8°, too small to obscure Venus. The witnesses' indications regarding the direction of the UFO were not precise enough to guarantee an exact match with Venus. However, the witnesses confirmed the absence of clouds and "starry weather." They observed to the west, at an altitude close to the mountains, and did not notice Venus, which is the most prominent star in that area of the sky (the other "bright" stars were Capella and Procyon, much less luminous, with a magnitude four points lower!), even though they referred to the size of a star to describe the final size of the UFO. If the UFO had been anything other than Venus, Venus would have been used to locate it. Other strange elements, such as the UFO moving away when lights were pointed at it or the watch running fast the next day, are pure coincidences that attracted the attention of witnesses due to the already prevailing atmosphere of strangeness. The above elements leave no room for doubt. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of Venus. These testimonies are somewhat imprecise in terms of information. They clearly illustrate the strangeness that a celestial body, in this case Venus, can generate, even for career military personnel.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere on the ground.
description: On April 27, 1980, a witness observed a strange phenomenon as he was about to return home around 12:30 a.m. A reddish-orange ball, about the size of a football, approached him and stopped about 5 meters from the house. This object shone brightly with a metallic sheen. Awakening other people in the house, they also observed this luminous ball. Frightened, they decided to go back to bed. The next day, no suspicious marks were noticed in front of the door. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Brief observation of an object falling: traces on the ground.
description: On April 21, 1980, at 11:55 AM, a witness heard a whistling sound and was frightened by a burst of flame and the fall of an object a few meters away from him, coming from the Northwest. He heard no impact noise and saw no smoke. This gardener described the object as being the size of a bucket, 20 cm in diameter, and rainbow-colored. The gendarmes called to the scene observed traces on the ground: within a 100-meter diameter circle, the ground was covered with a whitish powder, and the grass was scorched. No crater-type impact marks were present. The following day, a metallic piece was found. No record of the analysis results has been found in the GEIPAN archives, which leads to a C classification pending the recovery of these pieces.

summary: Sighting of flashing lights, probably an airplane.
description: On the evening of April 13, 1980, two people observed bright lights in the sky from their home. These lights moved rapidly at high altitude in a north-south direction and emitted a flashing white light. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information. However, it is likely that it was the passage of an aircraft at high altitude.

summary: Multiple and lengthy observations in various observation locations and while rolling a luminous phenomenon of color in the sky; "following ball illusion": observations of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification in an investigation report. This observation, previously classified as D and named SOULTZ SOUS FORETS (67) 1980, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On the night of April 11-12, 1980, between 11:50 PM and 12:30 AM, several witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky for an extended period from different locations. This phenomenon, whether stationary or moving as people travel in their vehicles, intrigues witnesses. The testimonies recorded in the police reports (Ne491 and Ne307) present the characteristics of a celestial body sighting. These characteristics are now well-known to GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) due to the accumulation of explained cases of this type, particularly over the last ten years (see www.geipan.fr and search for cases related to celestial phenomena such as Venus, the Moon, and the Sun): - observation duration of more than 30 minutes, low altitude in the sky, and eventual disappearance of the UFO behind the local terrain; - the UFO's position is stable when the witness is stationary and becomes mobile as soon as the witness moves, with the perception of being followed by the UFO. This is the "following sphere" illusion. The direction of the celestial body is, of course, absolutely fixed. When the car follows a roughly constant course, the celestial body is stationary relative to the vehicle and moves past the landscape. Since the witness had already been surprised by the appearance of the UFO and considered it to be at a close distance, this movement along the landscape is interpreted as the UFO moving parallel to the vehicle, reproducing the vehicle's speed, here to the left of the witnesses on the road from Hoelschloch to Merkwiller. And indeed, upon arriving in Merkwiller, the UFO "goes around the church" located to the left of the direction the car is traveling, and at the intersection, when the vehicle stops, the UFO remains at the intersection. - The witnesses did not identify a remarkable celestial body, despite its brightness, which was nevertheless present in the direction of observation, even though the sky was described as clear and starry. We verify that it is indeed a celestial body, namely Venus, which, at 23:50, is very visible (magnitude - 4.4) at azimuth 301° and altitude 6.2°. - The sighting locations of witnesses T2 and T3 agree; they place the UFO "above the Liebfrauenberg," which is in fact the castle of the same name. T1 uses a less precise reference point ("near the radars of the Drachenbronn base") and T3 mentions these same radars at the end of his statement, while reiterating that the UFO was above the Liebfrauenberg ("I specify that when the sphere was above the Liebfrauenberg, in this direction, it was very close to and just above the radar installations of the Air Base, to their left."). The wording is confusing, especially since there is a 20 to 30 arcsecond difference in azimuth between the two reference points (depending on the width of the domain attributed to the Liebfrauenberg). It is possible that T3 mainly wanted to draw attention to the fact that military radars were not far from the UFO. T4 mentions "we were able to observe the object for about half an hour; it was apparently hovering above the Drachenbronn base." Note that T4 is not not originally from the area (military service) and may have used the reference from T1 or T3 (the witnesses were all together at least at one point during the observation), which would be reflected in the "apparently," but while taking a shortcut, he is talking about the base, which is in a NE direction, and not the base's radars, which are in a Northwest-North direction. - taking the precise location used by T2 and T3 and not refuted by T1 and T4, namely the Liebfrauenberg castle and as the observation point the Merkwiller crossroads or the locality known as Hattenweg, the sighting corresponds to the azimuth of Venus (~300°). We verify that the altimetric profile in this direction (e +/- 5° around) does not obscure Venus, the highest obstacle (the Goersdorf forest massif) being located 4.2 km (from Hattenberg) with a difference in elevation of 200 m, i.e., at a relative elevation of 2.7e. According to this estimate, Venus was obscured at 0:20, while witnesses noted it at 0:25 or 0:30; the elevation variation over 10 minutes is 1.2e. This falls perfectly within the margins of error for assessing or knowing the exact times of the observation elements, as well as the precise positions of the witnesses at the time of these observations (which influences the assessment of the obscurations). The Gendarmerie report Ne491 notes in its investigation summary, and the accompanying diagram indicates, that the UFO made a final departure (after half an hour of stability above the Liebfrauenberg) towards the Northeast. This would contradict the hypothesis. However, T2 and T4 do not mention a final departure. The expression used by T2 states, "it remained above the Liebfrauenberg until 0:30. I don't know which direction it took." "After that, I didn't pay attention." This suggests that T2 was aware of reports of a final departure but was unable to confirm them. T3 mentions "this ball left, leaving a yellow trail, heading north." T3 may have experienced the classic illusion of a final reduction in the star's intensity (due to the atmospheric layer), interpreting it as a sudden decrease in distance, and he may have approximated a departure towards the northeast (Venus was then at 308 arcseconds) heading north, just as he was already approaching Liebfrauenberg and the base's radars. T1 indicates "The object remained stationary near the radars of the Drachenbronn base. We observed this phenomenon until 12:25 a.m., at which point it moved away at very high speed towards Lobsann. Lobsann being in the northeast, this indication would suggest a clear final departure of the UFO sharply to the right, without any possibility of to associate it with a flight in distance, as with T3. However, T1's testimony differs from the others on several points. In the car phase (with T2 and T4), T1 describes the UFO as "high in the sky," while T4 and T2 see it on the left (or in a fixed direction equivalent to the left), and T4 mentions that T1 signaled the UFO to the others on his left. T1 is the only one to describe a UFO as "two discs connected by a line." Finally, T1 describes the UFO crossing the road, the UFO coming from the right. This sensation of the UFO moving relative to the road could have occurred, but not in this direction and not to this extent. The road's heading is not stable, particularly at the cemetery (the area reported by T1 as the UFO crossing the road); the heading changes from north to northeast, and therefore the direction of Venus relative to the road changes from left (heading 10:00 AM) to align with the route's heading (heading 12:00). These elements of singularity and/or exaggeration of T1 sensations lead us to disregard them.
